Summary: Snow Crash, published in June 1992, is a science fiction novel by Neal Stephenson that blends cyberpunk, satire, and dystopian themes. The book explores the impact of corporate messaging, religion, and drug abuse on mass mind control through Sumerian language, with a focus on the elite software developers who understand the power of information. The novel is noted for its imaginative depiction of the metaverse and its blend of futuristic tech, dystopian world, Sumerian mythology, and computer science. It coined the term "Metaverse" and is considered a seminal work in the cyberpunk genre.

[1] Neal Stephenson's Snow Crash
    https://www.lithoguru.com/gentleman/essays/SnowCrash.html
    January 8, 2022

Snow Crash, published in 1992, is a science fiction novel that is part cyber punk, part satire, and a dystopian depiction of a near future. I was alternately engrossed and irritated by this thought-provoking and deeply flawed novel. [...] The core idea explored in the book relates to our ability to preserve the independence of our thinking. Corporate messaging, religion, and drug abuse have prepared the masses for mind control through Sumerian language babble that taps into our primitive minds. One group of people bright enough to avoid this fate, the elite, are software developers, the people that understand the power of information. But their life in the binary world makes them susceptible to a computer virus called Snow Crash [...] larger world. While I suspect most readers in the 1990s laughed at the extremes depicted in Snow Crash, in 2021 I did more cringing than laughing as the points hit close to home.
